business_model: Free HR-management SaaS monetized via insurance-brokerage commissions

historical_evidence.company: Founded 2013 by Parker Conrad and Laks Srini, offering free cloud-based HR software (onboarding, payroll integration, benefits management) monetized through insurance brokerage commissions on the benefits it helped administer.
historical_evidence.market: Large, underserved SMB HR/benefits-administration market with legacy, high-friction incumbents; the free-software-monetized-by-insurance-commission model was a genuinely novel wedge as of 2015.
historical_evidence.team: Founder Parker Conrad had prior startup experience (SigFig); by the Series C the company had scaled headcount rapidly to support its stated growth targets.
historical_evidence.product: Free, fast-to-deploy HR/benefits platform, differentiated primarily on price (free) and speed of setup relative to legacy brokers and HR software.
historical_evidence.execution: Extremely rapid funding progression: $15M Series A (January 2014) to a $66M Series B at a >$500M valuation (mid-2014) to a $500M Series C at a $4.5B valuation (May 6, 2015) — a 9x valuation step-up in roughly one year, among the fastest scaling trajectories publicly reported for a SaaS company at that time.
historical_evidence.traction: Publicly reported 2015 revenue guidance of over $50M for the year, up from approximately $8M in 2014 — a >6x year-over-year revenue growth claim reported contemporaneously by the company and covered without material contemporaneous challenge in the sources reviewed.
historical_evidence.financial: The company had publicly stated an ambition to reach $100M ARR by three years post-launch; the Series C was led by Fidelity and TPG, both sophisticated late-stage institutional investors, which is itself a meaningful signal of diligence having been performed at the time, however that diligence later turned out to have been insufficient (see future_outcome).
